newsitem.title: USA: Leach - reservations on mixing commerce, banking.
newsitem.headline: Leach - reservations on mixing commerce, banking.

text.p: House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach, R-Iowa, said Tuesday he has reservations on mixing commerce and banking.

"I believe in Glass-Steagall reform and a strong and competitive national bank charter, but have reservations about the administration's stated desire to mix commerce and banking and allow financial companies to integrate with commercial concerns," Leach said in a speech prepared for an investors' conference. Such a proposal would not be well-received by consumers, community bankers, small businesses and many in the House of Representatives, Leach said.
Leach said he intends to introduce a banking bill on the first day of the new Congress and to hold early hearings on what he called "a broad legislative initiative."
The bill would be based, with refinements, on House proposals toward the end of the last session on Glass-Steagall reform and charter conversion, Leach said.

The low national savings rate and the growth in mutual funds could mean "the country's banking system, especially community banks, could in the near future be facing a liquidity crisis, which the Federal Home Loan Banks are uniquely positioned to meet," Leach said.
